title: Why is it The Gambia?
subtitle: A small word with a long history: the country, the river and the name people use.

parts.text: The World Factbook calls the country The Gambia, while the country's capital is Banjul and the river running through it is the Gambia River.
The article is part of the country's name, not a description added by this site.

sections.title: A country shaped by a river

parts.text: The country follows the lower Gambia River inland from the Atlantic coast, and its modern borders leave it surrounded by Senegal except at the coast.
That geography is why the name is easy to flatten into a joke or a grammar correction, even though it points to a specific place and history.
A map name cannot tell us how people in The Gambia pronounce, translate or explain the country's name in their own languages. That part belongs here to people who live there.
